prompt: Each backend server is slow 1% of the time. A search request fans out to 100 of them and waits for all.
why: 1 − 0.99¹⁰⁰ ≈ 63% of requests hit at least one slow server. The tail becomes typical.
trap: Average latency looks fine; the fan-out exposes the tail.

prompt: To cut p99, a client sends a second copy of a request to another replica if the first hasn't answered within the p95 time.
why: Hedged requests trim the tail for a few percent extra load.
trap: Not a retry storm: the copy is sent only for the slowest few percent.

prompt: The dashboard shows average latency of 80 ms, yet users complain the app often feels slow. Pages make about 20 backend calls each.
why: With 20 calls per page, most pages hit some call's p95 or p99. Watch percentiles, not averages.
trap: Averages hide the slow calls that define the user's experience.

prompt: A dashboard query merges results from 40 shards. One shard with an overloaded disk makes every dashboard slow.
why: When you wait for all parts, the slowest part sets the response time.
trap: The overloaded disk is a knee problem on one shard; the fan-out is why everyone feels it.

prompt: A request passes through 10 services in sequence, each with p99 of 50 ms. The end-to-end p99 is far worse than anyone expected.
why: Each hop adds a chance of hitting its tail; with 10 hops, about 1 in 10 requests hits at least one slow step.

prompt: Average latency is 15 ms, but every few seconds a garbage collection pause makes a handful of requests take 400 ms.
why: The average hides rare long pauses that users at scale hit constantly.
trap: GC is the cause; the principle is that rare slow events dominate at scale.

prompt: A storage system sends each read to two replicas, and whichever starts first tells the other to cancel. Tail latency drops with almost no extra load.
tells: sends each read to two replicas
why: Tied requests cut the tail by racing replicas while cancellation keeps the extra work small.
trap: Replication here serves latency, not consistency.

prompt: A product page waits for all 30 thumbnails before showing, and one slow image host makes the whole page feel sluggish.
why: Waiting on many requests means the slowest one sets the pace.
trap: Show partial results or set deadlines so one straggler can't hold the page.
